notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: On 17 November Nvidia reported revenue up 103% and a further $150bn buyback, while its board refused Jensen Huang's return and set up an export-control committee, Washington proposed extending AI chip controls to Southeast Asia, Singapore defended its standing and the Singaporean firm Megaspeed is under US inquiry. In the two days before Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen on 19 November, Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge twice, Russia hit Kyiv's Yuzhny and Severny bridges and left 700,000 households without power and heating, and the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian attacks on Bahrain. France counted 146,000 at a new protest round against living costs on 17 November, after 270,000 on 6 November, and France has brought forward a minimum wage rise while Italy's coalition argues over 300 euros for pensioners. Apple blamed an outage on its own update, the NSA's classified network went down, South Korea's National Security Office met over a critical Java flaw and a cyberattack hit 178 brands including HSBC, Zoom and IKEA. Anthropic is reported pricing its share listing at the top of its range or higher, with several orders of $10 billion or more.
moved: The Nvidia thread was resumed on 17 November after one edition without a narrative, and moved from a dispute between Treasury and Commerce to new duties on the states the chips pass through, as Nvidia reported its best quarter. A 10 November expectation of a US chip rule with the Nvidia affair named was kept, by Handelsblatt and Fortune; separately, the expectation that Anthropic would cut or delay its listing failed.

The strikes thread was resumed on 17 November and moved from bases, ships and oil sites to crossings: the Crimean Bridge, Kyiv's bridges, a rail line to Hungary and Iran's Qeshm Island. The US strike on Qeshm reverses the Chronicle's reading that the Iran war had moved from fighting to talks.

The outage thread widened on 17 November to Apple, the NSA's classified network, a Java flaw and a cyberattack on 178 brands, and turned from who keeps the backup to whether a fault can be told from an attack. Its own case against says Apple named its cause within the day.

A thread began on Europe's weekly protests over prices and rents, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days. It takes in the same French protest rounds as the incomes thread, read as met by income top-ups.
silent: Governments setting pump prices turned silent on 17 November, with no narrative since 12 November; its expectations on Indonesian ferries and fuel freezes run to 8 and 10 December, so the quiet is more likely the editions' choice than governments letting go of prices.

Seats and entry used as pressure turned silent on 17 November. Its single-negotiator expectation failed on 13 November and its ground passed to the thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere, so the quiet is partly the reading failing, not only the sample.
Leaders' children judged turned silent on 17 November; no headline here has carried Gibran or Sara Duterte since 12 November, which may be the sample after the ASEAN summit coverage.

The Iran war thread stays silent, though its events came on 17 November in the strikes thread: the US struck Qeshm after Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait intercepted drones. That is the editions' division, not the war ending.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, talks and reach
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations. From 27 October to 5 November it followed the Hormuz price shock to jet fuel, mortgages, wages and rates, though no midterm report by 10 November named fuel prices. The war was reported paused on 8 November; on 10 November oil fell on talk of talks; on 11 November producers invested as if Hormuz would stay unsafe. Since then its events have come in other threads: a mine and a claimed strike on a US radar in Bahrain on 13 November, a Dutch fertiliser shortage blamed on the blockade on 14 November, and on 17 November a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian attacks on Bahrain. It is silent by the editions' division, not by the war's end.
threads.direction: After a pause reported on 8 November and a turn to talks and a falling price, by 17 November the US and Iran were reported striking each other again, at Bahrain and Qeshm, while talks were said to continue.

threads.label: Governments setting pump prices mid-war
threads.text: Begun on 7 November: Italy would not extend its diesel excise cut, Portugal adjusted its fuel tax discount and Taiwan's CPC held pump prices after absorbing NT$34.07 billion, joined as governments handing the war's fuel price back to drivers. After four editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 12 November with an unlinked narrative marked firm: Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a bill freezing fuel prices until February, Greece set €32 million for islanders' sea transport and Indonesian ferry operators asked to raise fares, with crude below $90. Its case against says the decisions move in different directions and none names Hormuz. No narrative carried it on 13, 14 or 17 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to early December.
threads.direction: It has moved from governments ending fuel tax cuts to governments keeping pump prices in their own hands and paying the gap from budgets as crude fell below $90.

threads.label: War energy shock turned into equipment orders
threads.text: Begun on 6 November and not linked by its edition to the Iran thread, though it starts from the same war. Iran says two tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Siemens Energy says a Middle East power push is straining gas turbine supply, a Chinese solar cell line runs at full capacity, Adani Green turns to batteries for India's grid, and an agency finds the energy crisis speeding renewables in emerging economies. The join is that buyers who cannot lower the price of imported fuel are buying equipment to need less of it. Its case against says Siemens Energy's backlog and China's solar capacity predate the war. No narrative has carried it since 6 November, so it is silent. Gas sought beside electrification began a separate thread on 10 November.

threads.label: Housing: state drives, outside money and work
threads.text: On 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing with Portugal investigating police at housing protests. On 6 November the Chronicle revived it, by judgment, when foreign buyers made 16% of Portuguese purchases as prices hit records. On 11 November it was revived again, by judgment, with a narrative marked tentative: millions of Spaniards struck over housing three weeks before a general election, a rush of withdrawals hit China's payroll housing fund, and employer-linked homes were offered in Tianhe and Taiwan. Its case against says Spain has a shortage and China a slump. On 17 November Spain's strike and Porto's housing camp came in a new thread on Europe's weekly protests, which joins them with wages and prices; the Chronicle has not revived this thread for it.
threads.direction: It has moved from states building homes, to prices set by buyers from outside, to housing argued over through strikes, payroll funds and employers.

threads.label: AI spending, then shared systems failing
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand. It ran through AI-led US growth, Taiwan's state buying, borrowing and a Nasdaq fall on 5 November, then the Nvidia case from 10 to 12 November, which moved to its own thread on 13 November. On 12 and 13 November a Microsoft outage stopped email at British councils and Australia's federal police, beside the FAA halting every US flight; on 14 November the fallback was reported left to households, with the Bank of Portugal advising cash at home. On 17 November, marked tentative, it widened to an Apple outage blamed on Apple's own update, the NSA's classified network going down, a Java flaw patched as an emergency in Seoul and Washington, and a cyberattack on 178 brands, read as faults and attacks hard to tell apart. Its own case against says Apple named its cause within the day.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and borrowing to Nvidia's weight, then to public services stopping when one system fails, to who holds the backup, and by 17 November to whether a fault can be told from an attack.

threads.label: Chip suppliers buying stakes in AI labs
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 10 November and not linked by its edition to the AI spending thread, whose ground it shares. TSMC is reported investing NT$32 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic as Anthropic's draft prospectus shows a listing of up to $64.4 billion, and CoreWeave's shares stand 65% below their peak. The join is a supplier buying into the customers whose spending fills its order book. Its case against says NT$32 billion is about $1 billion and chipmakers have long run venture arms. On 17 November its expectation that Anthropic would cut or delay its listing failed: nbd.com.cn and Yicai reported pricing at the upper end of the range or higher, with several orders of $10 billion or more. That is a reason to doubt the narrative's picture of labs turning to markets under strain. It is silent.

threads.label: Vote counts, rolls and election bodies contested
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with Flávio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil's president, Eisenkot accusing Netanyahu of delegitimising Israel's result and deletion forms in Delhi. On 2 November it took in Likud's doubt over the Knesset result, then moved before the vote: the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to halt California's count of 20,000 mail ballots, and India's roll revision removed more than 90,000 names in Chamarajanagar. On 4 November a narrative placed here by the Chronicle moved it to election bodies in Mexico, Nigeria, South Africa and Israel. On 6 November, with no narrative, Trump was reported calling the US election rigged and demanding victory in Alaska's Senate race. No narrative has carried it since 4 November; the expectation of a court request over a second state ran to 17 November and is not reported kept by these headlines.
threads.direction: It moved from disputing results to acting before polling and to who runs the commissions, and after the US vote a disputed result returned, by these headlines, without a narrative.

threads.label: Courts and heads of state given the last word
threads.text: Begun on 1 November and marked tentative: Poland's president and Tusk's government fighting over the Constitutional Tribunal, Egypt's debate on amending the constitution and Madeira's revision; its case against said only Poland's was a crisis. After six editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 7 November, by judgment, with an unlinked narrative also marked tentative. Lawyers say Vučić's pardons could go to Serbian courts and Strasbourg, Malaysia's Attorney General seeks an audience with the King over Najib Razak's conditional pardon, Taiwan's cabinet refuses to countersign an Elderly Welfare Act, and a Nigerian court voids Atiku's candidature. Its case against says the acts share form but not content. No narrative has carried it since 7 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It moved from fights over who controls courts and constitutions to who has the last word on pardons and laws already passed.

threads.label: Hacks through suppliers on freezers and wallets
threads.text: Begun late on 2 November with attacks on shop refrigeration hitting 17 Dutch businesses, which the EU called an attack on food supply, and North Korea denying the $6.3 billion Binance theft. On 3 November the join moved to how attackers get in: a fake job interview behind the Binance theft, Singapore Airlines records reached through Amadeus, and Italian advice to check supplier contacts as the attacks reached Belgium and Greece. On 10 November France was reported officially accusing Iran of the refrigeration attacks, and that evening the attacks were carried in the Iran thread. Later attacks came in the outage thread: a Brazilian insurer and Pix keys on 12 and 13 November, and a cyberattack on 178 brands on 17 November. The contractor expectation is open to 24 November.
threads.direction: It moved from what was hit, freezers and wallets, to the suppliers and staff through whom attackers got in, then fell silent as its refrigeration attacks passed to the Iran thread.

threads.label: Unclaimed threats against Poland and its answers
threads.text: Begun on 3 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Emailed bomb threats forced a plane to land in Warsaw and diverted two Poland-bound planes from London. A second person was detained over the arson of a Starlink station, Onet reports Kaliningrad becoming a centre of electronic warfare, and GROM special forces were sent to the Russian border. The join is cheap, unclaimed acts drawing costly answers below the level at which NATO's treaty applies. On 5 November an emailed bomb alert on a Milan-Warsaw flight kept the expectation of another such threat. On 17 November Onet's report of 8,000 false bomb alarms at European schools and airports came in the outage thread, not here. No narrative has carried it since 3 November, and no headline yet names Russia.

threads.label: Chinese makers' gains and others' answers
threads.text: Begun on 3 November: SCG's chief executive called China's cheap exports a fact of life, Thailand raised taxes on imported electric cars, and Tata Motors and Iveco formed a group. It was revived on 7 November, by judgment, when Musk said Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck and BYD's Yangwang opened pre-orders for a 2.08 million yuan car. On 8 November its own edition carried it on, with Tesla suspending orders for the Cybertruck's entry version, NIO claiming a car a minute and Yangwang launching in Abu Dhabi. On 10 November, with no narrative, The Independent reported Musk axing the Cybertruck with refunds, keeping the 7 November expectation of another US carmaker cutting an electric pickup, though by Tesla itself. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, and no headline here reports a sale lost to a Chinese maker.
threads.direction: It moved from producers elsewhere merging or taxing to meet Chinese goods, to producers elsewhere retreating, and by 8 November to Chinese makers selling abroad at both the cheap and the luxury end.

threads.label: Foreign capitals reading the US midterm result
threads.text: Begun on 4 November, the day after the midterms. Iran's leaders called the result a rejection of Trump's war, while Khamenei said Washington's Iran policy would not change. Egyptian commentators named Netanyahu among the losers, Pedro Sánchez said it would help Spain's socialists, Canada's National Post asked whether Trump still wants a deal, and Polish analysts expected no change in foreign policy. The join is that each capital reads the vote through its own dispute with Washington, while the president still runs foreign policy. On 12 November, with no narrative, Diário do Grande ABC and Dân trí reported Trump threatening to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop migrant caravans, keeping the 4 November expectation of a tariff threat against an ally. No narrative has carried it since 4 November.

threads.label: Who answers for AI systems' errors
threads.text: Begun on 4 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Sina reports Accenture accused of publishing papers full of AI hallucinations after dismissing staff who would not use AI. Google has switched AI tools off by default for school pupils, and an Italian trial of AI found it not chargeable but socially dangerous. Portuguese firms adopt AI faster than they train staff, Anthropic's IPO filing sets out the risks of its build, and NTT adds AI defences as attacks rise sevenfold. The join is that the consequences of errors land on whoever took a system up. Its case against says the Italian trial may be a staged debate and the Accenture item is an accusation. No narrative has carried it since 4 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Parliaments refusing governments' budgets
threads.text: Begun on 5 November. French deputies unanimously rejected their government's budget ahead of nationwide wage strikes, and Senegal's parliament asked for the 2027 budget bill to be withdrawn. Rob Jetten warned Dutch MPs that voting down his tax plan would cost billions, Japan's prime minister faces a time-limited committee session over a consumption tax cut, and a Democratic Congress must now fund the US government. The join is that governments no longer command the chambers that pass next year's taxes and spending. Its case against says autumn is budget season, first-reading rejections are common, and only the French and Senegalese cases are outright refusals. No narrative has carried it since 5 November, so it is silent; the Japanese cut bears on an expectation open to 28 November.

threads.label: Soldiers sent to keep civil order
threads.text: Begun on 5 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Indonesia's armed forces commander put troops in Jakarta, and the army gave its own account of a deadly riot at a Maulid celebration in Aceh. Pakistan deployed the army and Rangers for Punjab by-elections, a Bangladeshi soldier was killed raiding traffickers at Teknaf, and Lebanon's army ran raids and checkpoints with dozens arrested. A French bill widening when police may fire was called an advance by police unions and a licence to kill by the left. The join is civil order handed to soldiers or to rules closer to theirs. Its case against says Pakistan's and Lebanon's arrangements are long-standing and the tasks differ. No narrative has carried it since 5 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Regulators targeting platforms' recommendation systems
threads.text: Begun on 6 November. The European Commission accused TikTok of breaching EU rules through its content recommendation system, and Google, Meta and TikTok are suing to block a California law restricting addictive social media features for children. China's broadcasting regulator opened a two-month campaign against vulgar and homogenised AI micro-dramas after removing 75,000 titles, and Democrats are preparing AI bills for Congress. The join is that the thing regulated is the system choosing what a user sees next, not a single post. Its case against says the three regulators want different things and only the EU and California cases are clearly about ranking design. No narrative has carried it since 6 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Failed banks and money cases reaching office
threads.text: Begun on 6 November. Paraguay's Congress resumed impeachment of President Santiago Peña over the Ueno bank crisis, Daniel Vorcaro's phone recorded 316 interactions with Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the Banco Master case, and UMNO's move to pay Najib Razak's RM50 million fine split Malaysia's coalition. On 8 November an unlinked narrative, placed here by the Chronicle, reported a court freezing the assets of Peña, described as former president, and his arrest over an estimated $809 million Ueno loss, with the Philippine vice-president answering wealth charges and opponents in Armenia and Egypt facing courts. No narrative has carried it since 8 November. On 12 November Sara Duterte's impeachment trial appeared in the new thread on leaders' children.
threads.direction: It moved from failed banks reaching people in office to courts reaching office-holders through money in general, with Peña going from impeachment proceedings to arrest in two days.

threads.label: El Niño's first weeks arriving as rain
threads.text: Begun on 7 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Keiko Fujimori is reported visiting parts of Peru's Tumbes hit by rain, and Pulzo reports that El Niño has not stopped thunderstorms and hail in Bogotá. La Patria reports a landslide bringing trees down onto an avenue in Manizales, Brazil's Civil Defence has a 72-hour alert out, and a downpour stopped Formula One qualifying at Interlagos. The join is that an El Niño expected as drought is arriving first as rain. Its case against says October and November are wet seasons in Colombia and south-eastern Brazil in any year, only one headline names El Niño, and only the Tumbes rain is out of season. No narrative has carried it since 7 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Routes to work abroad rationed and deadly
threads.text: Begun on 8 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Off Lompoul in northern Senegal a pirogue capsized and at least 21 people died. In Bangladesh a lottery shortlisted 300 applicants for 112 fee-free jobs in Malaysia. A testimony in Portugal's SAPO describes shared rooms and low pay ending a migrant's stay, and in West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari promised to deport every 'Bangladeshi infiltrator'. The join is that a person's attempt to work abroad is rationed by a draw, the sea, wages or expulsion. Its case against says the lottery may be meant to cut out recruitment agents, the shipwreck's destination is not given, and four of seven headlines come from bdnews24. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Gas supply sought beside climate summit targets
threads.text: Begun on 10 November and marked tentative by its own edition. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed the last four years as the hottest on record, and COP31 set out an electrification push as the 1.5C goal slips. Deutsche Welle examined Germany's untapped gas, Japan's and Vietnam's leaders discussed an early start to an LNG project, Argentina awaited $38 billion of investment decisions for Vaca Muerta, and Brazil extended its household cooking gas programme to 2031. The join is governments securing gas while planning to electrify. Its case against says Vaca Muerta and the LNG talks are long-running. No narrative has carried it since 10 November, so it is silent; COP31 in Antalya appeared on 11 November only in the seats thread, over Israel's exclusion.

threads.label: Ukraine talks and who pays in Europe
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 10 November and marked firm by its edition. US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced a planned prisoner exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 a side and a US offer of 'NATO-style' security guarantees with $400 million in weapons, while Merz threatened to block the next EU budget unless every member supports Ukraine and Fico called that blackmail. Its case against says Merz's demand may belong to the 2028 to 2034 budget talks. On 11 and 12 November the talks came in the seats thread, on 13 and 17 November in the strikes thread, and on 14 November in a thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere. No narrative has carried the question of who pays since 10 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Pope Leo in politics, restraint on reform
threads.text: Begun on 11 November. Pope Leo XIV left Argentina after a Mass for three million, with Die Welt reporting that Javier Milei is on his own after the Pope's criticism, and arrived in Peru, where the government declared non-working days and Keiko Fujimori invited guests to meet him. In the same days the Vatican halted the reform process in the German diocese of Speyer. The join is one office speaking against a government's policy in South America while limiting lay-led reform in Germany. Its case against says popes have criticised Argentine economic policy for a decade, a diocese without a bishop cannot normally change its own structures, and host governments always declare holidays for papal visits. No narrative has carried it since 11 November, so it is silent; the Peru expectation runs to 20 November.

threads.label: Seats, borders and talks used as pressure
threads.text: Begun on 11 November and marked tentative: the CSTO stripped Armenia of its vote, Turkey excluded Israel from COP31 in Antalya, and Washington and Moscow asked Europe to choose one negotiator for the Ukraine talks. On 12 November it was carried on as entry of every kind: Israel will bar Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Washington's envoys said Europeans would join the next round, and Putin spoke of US visas for Russian Olympians. On 13 November the single-negotiator expectation failed when the EU agreed a team of five countries and EU institutions, which weakens the reading of entry as a bargaining move. Its ground passed on 14 November to the thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere. No narrative carried it on 13, 14 or 17 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It moved from seats in alliances and summits to entry of every kind, and on 13 November Europe was admitted to the Ukraine talks on its own terms, against the thread's reading.

threads.label: Leaders' children judged on their own conduct
threads.text: Begun on 12 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice-president over a certificate scandal, Sara Duterte's impeachment trial in the Philippines is to resume after the ASEAN summit, Donald Trump Jr left an adviser's role at the prediction market Kalshi over a conflict with a rival investment, and Nigeria's president congratulated his son Seyi on a traditional title in Kebbi before his own 2027 campaign. The join is what a leader's name entitles a child to hold. Its case against says the cases share a family tie and little else, Seyi Tinubu faces no allegation, and two stories come from South-East Asia during the ASEAN summit. No narrative carried it on 13, 14 or 17 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Nvidia scandal as a chip export enforcement dispute
threads.text: Begun on 13 November with a narrative marked firm that continues nothing, though the Nvidia case ran in the AI spending thread from 10 to 12 November: Bessent blamed Lutnick for Megaspeed not being blacklisted, and the Senate summoned Huang and Lutnick. After no narrative on 14 November it was resumed on 17 November, marked plausible. Nvidia reported revenue up 103% and a $150bn buyback, its board refused Huang's return and set up an export-control committee, and Huang will testify to the House on 1 December. Washington proposed extending AI chip controls to Southeast Asia, Singapore defended its standing and Megaspeed is under US inquiry, keeping a 10 November expectation of a US chip rule with the Nvidia affair named. Its case against says diversion through Singapore and Malaysia was known before, and Nvidia's quarter reflects old orders.
threads.direction: It has moved from a dispute between two US departments over who let chips reach China to new duties on the states and firms the chips pass through, while Nvidia's sales grew.

threads.label: Long-range strikes during Russia and Iran talks
threads.text: Begun on 13 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing: as the EU named its team for the Ukraine talks, a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, bombs went off in Moscow and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain. After no narrative on 14 November it was resumed on 17 November, marked tentative, with crossings as the targets: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge two days running, Russia hit Kyiv's Yuzhny and Severny bridges and left 700,000 households without power, a strike on Transcarpathia led Hungary to restrict trains to Mukachevo, and the US struck Qeshm after Iranian attacks on Bahrain, two days before Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen. Its case against says Russia has hit Ukraine's heating every winter since 2022 and the US called Qeshm self-defence.
threads.direction: It has moved from strikes on bases, ships and oil sites far from the fronts to strikes on bridges and islands in the days before the 19 November meeting.

threads.label: Europe's security bargained in talks it does not lead
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing, sharing ground with the seats thread, whose expectation of a single EU negotiator failed on 13 November, and with the strikes thread. Zelensky said Washington floated Ukraine giving up Donbas in return for NATO membership, the Kremlin announced that Putin, Xi and Trump will meet on 19 November, and Russian officials demanded that Britain give up its nuclear cover for Europe. The join is that the subjects of Moscow's December 2021 draft treaties are raised in a format led by the US, Russia and China. Its case against says the US idea is known only from Zelensky. No narrative carried it on 17 November, when the meeting was reported fixed for Shenzhen in the strikes thread's narrative; its expectations on the meeting run to 24 and 25 November.

threads.label: Incomes set by rule falling behind prices
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. France had a fifth Saturday of protests against the cost of living and French police demanded a higher risk allowance; an Italian simulation put a 2028 pension more than 13,000 euros a year below one of twenty years earlier; a former Argentine judge warned of delays in retirees' claims, and a Canadian disability charity closed. The join is incomes fixed by law, decree or grant falling behind prices; its case against says the events share no cause. On 17 November a new thread on Europe's weekly protests took in the same French protest rounds and read them as met by top-ups, France's minimum wage rise brought forward on 10 November and Italy's argument over 300 euros for pensioners. The Chronicle has kept the two apart, as the newer narrative was built from its own notebook subject.

threads.label: Governments taking back roles in food supply
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Nieuws.nl reports a fertiliser shortage caused by the Hormuz blockade threatening Dutch food security, Marib's farmers in Yemen have harvests and no open markets, Senegal calls rice a pillar of food sovereignty, New York is spending $70 million on five city-run grocery stores, Egypt's prime minister inspects a permanent state food fair, and Fortune reports nearby shops losing sales when Walmart leaves a town. The join is public authorities taking back choosing what is grown, securing inputs and selling food. Its case against says only the fertiliser story is new, Egypt's outlets date from the 1940s and New York's stores were a 2025 election promise. No narrative carried it on 17 November; its expectations run to 5 and 12 December.

threads.label: Europe's protests over prices, met by top-ups
threads.text: Begun on 17 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts two weeks of protest over living costs and housing: 270,000 marched outside Paris on 6 November, Porto's housing camp put up tents on 8 November, Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on 11 November, Italy carried out searches in 13 cities on 14 November, and France counted 146,000 at a new round on 17 November. France brought forward a minimum wage rise and Italy's coalition argues over 300 euros for pensioners, while the Commission says the energy shock still raises prices. Its case against says Spanish rents and French wages have different causes. It shares France with the incomes thread and Spain with the silent housing thread.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war thread had turned to which governments carry the fuel price and which take more of it as revenue, with US-Iran talks stuck.
withdrawn.undone: On 2 November no fuel-tax argument appeared, Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well and the thread was about whether a strike or talks follow the US vote. The who-pays reading rested on Turkey's single tax rise and is not carried as the direction; its expectation of a second government raising a fuel tax is still open.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread had turned to how narrowly the gains land, on a few chip and computing makers and their staff.
withdrawn.undone: Late on 2 November the thread was about the build depending on borrowing, with Oracle and Meta raising about $20 billion each and Anthropic losing more than its revenue, and on governments and voters setting terms for data centres; no payouts were reported. The concentration reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the direction; its expectations stay open.

withdrawn.held: Late on 2 November the Iran thread was tilting towards talks, with prices falling on leaders' words while incidents at sea continued.
withdrawn.undone: On 3 November the edition reported the strait still shut as the US struck Iran, with a bombing at Qeshm on polling day; Qatar's mediation went on, but the force was American, not only incidents at sea. The talks tilt held for one edition, and the thread returned to who pays and who gains from the closure.

withdrawn.held: Central banks abroad, Brazil's among them with the world's highest real interest rate, were holding rates high against the Iran war's oil price.
withdrawn.undone: On 5 November Mexico's central bank cut to 6.25% and Brazil's continued to cut while the Bank of England raised to 4%. Holding high describes some importers, not rate-setters in general, and the Mexican and Brazilian headlines do not name the war.

withdrawn.held: The contested-count thread had moved on from disputing results after a vote to acting before polling and contesting the bodies that run elections.
withdrawn.undone: On 6 November Liputan6 reported Trump saying the US election was rigged and Svenska Yle reported him demanding victory in Alaska's close Senate race. Disputing a result after the vote is back in these headlines, so the thread has not left it behind.

withdrawn.held: On 7 November the US-Iran war was going on, with the US reported striking Iran again and the Revolutionary Guards saying their missile range limits were lifted.
withdrawn.undone: On 8 November the edition reported the war as paused, with Trump calling a return to it very unlikely and pressure moved to Iraq's border crossings and a naval build-up. The fighting reported that day was between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, not between the US and Iran.

withdrawn.held: Since 3 November the Iran thread had been following who pays for the war's oil price, a question that passed on 7 November to the thread on fuel tax cuts.
withdrawn.undone: On 8 November the thread's narrative named no price, rate or tax, and followed pressure on Iran by land and sea and the Saudi-Houthi exchange. The price question is not carried as this thread's direction; it sits in the fuel tax thread.

withdrawn.held: On 8 November the question of the war's oil price had left the Iran thread and sat in the fuel tax thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the Iran thread's own narrative turned on price: Brent fell 5 per cent on Trump's words about talks, and exporters in Kenya and drivers in Vietnam were reported carrying the war's cost.

withdrawn.held: On 8 November the Iran thread was moving towards containing Iran by its land border with Iraq and a naval build-up.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the blockade was reported continuing, but the thread's narrative led with Trump's talk of momentum after meeting Qatar's prime minister and the oil price falling on it. No headline reported Iraq closing a crossing.

withdrawn.held: The reading of AI spending as gains concentrated on a few chip makers rested on one edition and was not carried as the thread's direction.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the thread returned on that reading: so much rests on Nvidia that Jensen Huang's admitted affair with an alleged spy moved its shares 8 to 9 per cent and US chip policy. The concentration reading now has two editions behind it.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread was moving from profit and borrowing to the market risk of resting so much on one chip firm, with share falls running on from 5 November.
withdrawn.undone: On the evening of 10 November its edition carried the Nvidia case on as espionage reached through people, beside a US officer arrested in Britain and leaked Norwegian phone numbers, while the market side, TSMC's stakes in AI labs and Nvidia's 12 per cent fall, came in a narrative not linked to it. The thread has turned out to be two.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise had reached the US ballot and cost Trump's party Congress.
withdrawn.undone: By 10 November no report on the midterm results or exit polls in these collections named fuel or energy prices as a reason, failing a 1 November expectation. The link rested on the 4 November narrative and on Trump tying the defeat to the war, not to the price.

withdrawn.held: The Nvidia case had passed from market risk to espionage reached through people, with the money side split off into a separate thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 12 November Huang's resignation was read as a risk of concentration on a few American suppliers, with AI shares falling from Bangkok to New York and Taiwan's suppliers counting the cost. The money side is back in the AI spending thread.

withdrawn.held: Governments were handing the war's fuel price back to drivers while the war went on, as Italy and Portugal ended or adjusted fuel tax discounts.
withdrawn.undone: On 12 November Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a fuel price freeze to February and Greece paid €32 million toward island shipping costs. Governments were reported keeping pump prices in their own hands, not handing them back.

withdrawn.held: Huang's resignation and the Microsoft 365 outage were one thread about how much rests on a few American suppliers.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November the edition gave Nvidia its own narrative, as a dispute between Treasury and Commerce over chips reaching China, and carried the outage on as public services running on single systems, beside the FAA's nationwide halt, which is a state system, not a supplier's.

withdrawn.held: Washington and Moscow were using Europe's place at the Ukraine talks as pressure, offering it on condition that Europe choose one negotiator.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November the EU agreed to be represented by a team of five countries and EU institutions, joined by the coalition of the willing, and is joining the talks. The 11 November expectation of a single envoy failed, and the condition did not hold.

withdrawn.held: Since 8 November the Iran war had moved from fighting between the US and Iran to talks and a falling price.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain, and on 17 November the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian attacks on Bahrain. The US and Iran are reported striking each other again while talks are said to continue.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on twenty-four editions over about three weeks, with none stamped 28 October, 9 November, 15 or 16 November, drawn from whichever publishers the collection reads and capped in how many headlines each may supply, with four narratives today. Two of today's four narratives resume threads after a single missing edition, and a third continues the outage thread, so continuity is again partly produced by a brief that asks each edition to say what it carries on; the protests narrative was built from a notebook subject, so its two-week run was assembled by the site before any narrative tested it. I kept that narrative apart from the incomes thread, though both count the same French protest rounds, and a reader could fairly call them one. The withdrawal of the Iran thread's turn to talks rests on two strikes, one of which the US called self-defence. The crossings narrative's own case against says two wars produce strikes every day and only timing before Shenzhen joins them; the outage narrative's says Apple named its cause within the day; and Nvidia's quarter reflects orders placed before the scandal. The pull of my own earlier framing of single systems failing shaped how I carried the outage thread into attribution, and the one kept expectation today, on chip rules, was set by a narrative the Chronicle has since moved out of the thread it now confirms.
line: On 17 November 2026, two days before Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen, Ukraine strikes the Crimean Bridge again and the US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island.
revision: One thread began, on Europe's weekly protests over prices and rents, built from a notebook subject; the Nvidia and strikes threads were revived after one edition without a narrative, and the fuel price, seats and leaders' children threads turned silent under the three-edition rule. The Iran thread's direction from fighting to talks was withdrawn after the US strike on Qeshm, the outage thread was relabelled as it turned to telling faults from attacks, and the standing was rewritten around chips, crossings struck before Shenzhen, protests and outages.
